The Blessing in the Wrong Envelope

装错信封的祝福 · 648 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1Before her marriage Mei asked two relatives for a short blessing. Her aunt had raised her after her parents divorced. Her father had married again and wanted to speak with his new wife. Mei's desire was an intimate ceremony, not a grand display. On the eve of the wedding, her fiance found two matching envelopes beside a candle. Her nephew had mistaken a heartfelt letter of remembrance for an invitation. He handed it to the wrong person.

2Mei's father read a line about devotion and took it as a criticism of his loyalty. His wife thought the tone was hostile. The aunt had written it to a widower in the family who was travelling to the luncheon. It recalled the companionship that brought them through sorrow. An uncle wanted to spare everyone's feelings by putting the letter away. Mei thought they could be more forgiving if they spoke before a private message set the mood for the wedding.

3Mei asked her stepmother to sit with her. She understood why her father was jealous, but resented being asked to settle their history in public. A sympathetic friend warned that an apology could sound like a pushy demand for forgiveness. Mei asked for a polite greeting to the aunt and an earnest word of encouragement. Her stepmother was receptive. She wanted her own role to feel supportive without making anyone accept a symbolic embrace.

4Upon hearing his fiancee from the hallway, the groom came inside. He asked whether the bride wanted him to change the seating or simply listen. Mei wished her beloved elder relatives could show affection without speaking for her. Her fiance's question helped her say that directly. An old family acquaintance had offered to read a sincere greeting at the ceremony. Mei decided to ask her father to give it himself, if he could do so respectfully.

5The aunt brought a second envelope. It held a token that Mei's mother had worn at her own engagement. She wanted Mei to inherit it, though she did not expect her to follow every customary rule. Mei's younger sibling asked why the two families could not give their blessings together. The preacher said they could, if each person was comfortable with the other hearing it. They moved two chairs closer and let the aunt decide which part of her letter could be read aloud.

6At the ceremony the bridegroom thanked their kin for their generosity. The aunt blessed the couple and described the joy of helping a child grow. Mei's father acknowledged her years of sacrifice. His manner was less formal than he had planned, and more fatherly. At the end of the solemnity he offered the aunt his arm. She accepted with a gracious smile. Both could pray for the couple without asking the guests to decide who had been right.

7At the banquet a cousin offered congratulations, then asked if the two women had always been close. Mei said they were still learning tolerance and harmony. The letter went back to its reader. A sister-in-law chose a joyous picture. It offered sympathy to the newlyweds without retelling a marital dispute. It showed both chairs. Mei liked it better than a photograph in which everyone was obliged to smile. The picture let the family cherish a rewarding moment without disguising an exhausting conversation.

8The next morning Mei's father wrote a note on a fresh card. He had meant to defend his place in her life. He left grateful that both families could share her happiness. An elder cousin and his girlfriend had set the chairs. Their father often held birthday meals where both families could meet. Mei thanked them. She could appreciate a respectful gesture without forgetting earlier grief. When her aunt came to collect the token, she asked whether their relationship felt different. Mei pointed to the card. They could now talk about it without beginning a quarrel.

四级汇总词汇 · 31中文译文

装错信封的祝福

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1婚礼前，梅请两位亲人各送上一段简短的祝福。父母离婚后，是姨妈把她带大的。父亲已经再婚，想和现在的妻子一起致辞。梅想办一场只有亲近的人参加的婚礼。婚礼前夜，未婚夫在蜡烛旁发现两个一模一样的信封。她的侄子把一封真情流露的怀念信当成了请柬，交错了人。

2父亲读到一句关于用心付出的话，以为是在指责自己不够忠诚。他的妻子也觉得那语气带着敌意。其实，姨妈把信写给了家里一位正在赶来参加午宴的鳏夫。信里回忆了两人如何相互陪伴、熬过悲伤。一位叔叔想把信收起来，免得谁都难受。梅觉得，在一封私信影响婚礼气氛之前，大家先说一说，也许就能多一分体谅。

3梅请继母坐在身边。她理解父亲为什么嫉妒，却不愿被要求当众评判他们的过去。一位体谅她的朋友提醒，道歉有时会让人觉得是在催对方原谅。梅只请继母礼貌地向姨妈问个好，再真诚地说一句鼓励的话。继母听了进去。她希望自己能帮上忙，也希望大家可以自己决定要不要用拥抱来表示和解。

4新郎在走廊里听见未婚妻的话，就走了进来。他问新娘是想让自己调换座位，还是只想找个人听她说。梅希望自己深爱的长辈表达关心时，也给她留一点自己开口的空间。未婚夫的问题让她把这句话直接说了出来。一位认识家里多年的熟人愿意在仪式上读一段真诚的祝词。梅决定先请父亲亲自念，前提是他能对姨妈保持尊重。

5姨妈又拿来一个信封，里面有一件梅的母亲订婚时戴过的纪念物。姨妈想把它传给梅，至于那些习俗，梅可以自己决定遵守哪些。梅年纪小一些的手足问，两家人为什么不能一起祝福。主持仪式的牧师说，只要彼此都愿意听，就可以。大家把两把椅子挪近，让姨妈自己选信里可以当众读的一段。

6仪式上，新郎感谢亲人们的慷慨。姨妈祝福两人，也说起陪伴一个孩子长大的喜悦。梅的父亲肯定了姨妈这些年的牺牲。他说得没有原先准备的那么正式，倒更像一位父亲。庄重的仪式结束时，他把手臂伸给姨妈，让她挽着。姨妈大方地笑着接受了。两人都可以为新人祈祷，宾客也可以安心地分享他们的祝福。

7婚宴上，一位表亲道了喜，又问两位女士是不是一直这么亲近。梅说，大家还在学着包容，学着和睦相处。信回到了收信人手里。一位姻亲选了一张喜庆的照片。照片传达了对新人的体谅，也把过去的婚姻纠纷留在了画面之外。照片里，两把椅子都在。梅更喜欢这一张，因为每个人都可以自然地笑或不笑。家人可以珍惜这个值得记住的时刻，也记得此前那场谈话有多费力。

8第二天早上，父亲找了一张新卡片写了几句话。他原本想维护自己在女儿生活中的位置，离开时却感激两家人都能分享她的幸福。那两把椅子是一位年长的表亲和他的女友摆的。他们的父亲也常办生日聚餐，方便两家人见面。梅向他们道谢。她可以珍惜别人善意的举动，也记得从前的悲伤。姨妈来取那件纪念物时，问她是否觉得彼此的关系变了。梅指了指卡片。如今，他们可以谈起这件事，谈话也不必从争吵开始。
